note: P6-04c multi-limb normalized long division. P0 = ca31bb9c (the P6-04a baseline), P1 = 8eb4decf.
verdict: clear success with one approved performance waiver: multi-limb 28.4x to 271.8x with every combination same-direction, allocations from O(numerator bits) to a constant 6, two JS shapes already inside the 2x second-stage target, and the one missed gate (mod-size-2x1) accepted as an explicit waiver rather than reported as a pass

commits.ad6bd639: normalize ownership transferred exactly once, plus the multi-limb fail-index OOM sweep
commits.8eb4decf: bit-at-a-time branch deleted and replaced by normalized limb division

mechanism.aligned_with: qjs js_bigint_divrem plus mp_divnorm (quickjs.c:11893-11976): normalize the divisor's top limb, estimate one quotient digit, correct against the second divisor limb, multiply-subtract, add back on overshoot
mechanism.deliberately_not_copied: qjs's top-quotient-limb 0-or-1 special case. Its JSBigInt is two's complement with sign extension so the top quotient limb can only be 0 or 1; zjs is normalized sign-magnitude where it is any u64. The mechanism is mirrored, the representation-specific case is not.
mechanism.no_shrinking_realloc: both results are sized exactly before allocation: the quotient's top digit is non-zero exactly when the numerator's leading nb limbs are at least the divisor, and the remainder's unshifted length is measured with a read-only helper before its buffer exists. A zero remainder allocates nothing.
mechanism.scratch: u and v stay as two separate allocations on purpose, so the topology stays readable and the OOM sweep can fail each independently; merging is left to P6-04d

allocation_topology.method: gdb silent breakpoints, slope between N=1 and N=21
allocation_topology.composition: 6 = two absCloneWithAllocator in divRemAlloc, u, v, quotient, remainder; independent of the numerator's width

direct_core.harness: four build instances per side, all sixteen combinations, three interleaved rounds
direct_core.shift_axis: P6-04a recorded this axis while it was inert because nothing normalized. It is live now, and flat: 147.0 ns at shift 0 to 153.1 ns at shift 63, a 4.2% span with no expensive step.

js_level.harness: four build instances per side, all sixteen combinations
js_level.attribution_note: div_8x1's 110.5x belongs to P6-04b, not this cut: P0 here is ca31bb9c, which predates it
js_level.second_stage_target: the 2x goal is already met on div_16x8 at 1.60x and mod_8x4 at 1.87x; div_8x4 is still 3.20x

single_limb_no_regression_gate.baseline: ad6bd639 (P6-04b plus the ownership fix), four instances, which is the correct denominator for this gate rather than ca31bb9c
single_limb_no_regression_gate.verdict: MISSED. mod-size-2x1 is the one shape with all sixteen combinations above 1.0 (range 1.0216 to 1.0672), a 3.5% geomean and 1.5 ns in absolute terms. div-size-1x1, div-size-2x1 and mod-size-1x1 all have ranges straddling 1.0, so they are noise. 8x1 and 16x1 are slightly faster at 0.991 to 0.997.
single_limb_no_regression_gate.cause: almost certainly code layout: divRemAbsAlloc went from two branches plus an inlined bit loop to two branches plus two noinline calls, moving the dispatcher's codegen
single_limb_no_regression_gate.not_chased: 1.5 ns per operation against 28x to 272x elsewhere; P6-04d will touch this dispatcher again if it merges the scratch allocations, and it should be re-measured then

waiver.status: approved explicit waiver, not a pass
waiver.statement: the regression is real, stable and does not meet the original gate: mod-size-2x1 at +3.47% geomean and +1.51 ns, all sixteen combinations above 1.0 with a lower bound of 1.0216
waiver.accepted_because: it is weighed against 28.7x to 271.8x on the multi-limb path
obligations: keep mod-size-2x1 as a permanent sentinel
every P6-04d cut must re-measure div/mod at 1x1, 2x1, 8x1 and 16x1
re-judge after P6-04d completes; if mod 2x1 still regresses above 1%, take a separate one-cut that inspects the dispatcher body and the single-limb helper's call placement
that cut must not re-inline the multi-limb algorithm and must not trade 8x1 or 16x1 away for this 1.5 ns

directed_vectors.test: normalized long division handles every quotient-estimate correction
directed_vectors.provenance: each vector was found by instrumenting the estimate loop with event counters, searching for triggering inputs, and freezing the input; the counters are not in the shipped code

events.add-back: three vectors, directed search - random differentials cannot reach it, roughly two in 2^64 and needing three or more divisor limbs for the two-limb correction to miss
events.clamped estimate: constructed by hand - needs the running window's top limb to equal the divisor's, built from a numerator whose leading two limbs are below the divisor but share its top limb, so the first digit is zero and leaves them in place

directed_vectors.assertions: q*b+r == a, abs(r) < abs(b), remainder sign, no leading zero limb, across all four sign combinations

correctness.shift_coverage: all 64 normalization shifts, not a sample of four, each crossed with nb 2-5 and na from nb to nb+3
correctness.relations: lhs < rhs, lhs == rhs, quotient 1, exact division, largest non-zero remainder

random_differential.bias: saturated, sparse, alternating, near 2^63, equal limb counts, one limb longer

correctness.oom_sweep: every allocation point failed in turn across all four sign combinations; each attempt returns the correct result or OutOfMemory with no outstanding allocation and the caller's operand limbs unmodified; a separate mode fails every shrinking realloc, refusing both the remap and the alloc-and-copy fallback, and the runtime keeps working afterwards
correctness.force_gc_cross_engine: the 487-line probe and the 20000-case differential are both byte-identical to qjs under force-GC

correction_to_P6_04b.claim_being_corrected: P6-04b recorded divRemAbsAlloc's normalize ownership problem as a pre-existing double free that test-oom did not reach
correction_to_P6_04b.measurement: instrumented, the two tail normalize calls shrink 0 times in 2001 divisions: subAbsAlloc normalizes the remainder every iteration and setBit leaves the quotient's top limb non-zero, so the failing branch is dead
correction_to_P6_04b.correct_statement: ad6bd639 hardens an unsound ownership pattern rather than fixing a live defect, and the fail-index sweep is a forward OOM contract rather than a regression test

gates.single_limb_no_stable_regression: MISSED on mod-size-2x1 at +3.5% geomean, 1.5 ns absolute, all sixteen combinations above 1.0 - accepted as an approved explicit waiver, not a pass
gates.overall: clear success with an approved waiver on the single-limb gate

limits: the 1.6-3.5% regression on the smallest single-limb shapes was not chased and the gate is missed
u and v remain two separate scratch allocations by design; merging is P6-04d
no reciprocal precomputation, Burnikel-Ziegler, Newton reciprocal, quotient/remainder FAM or combined scratch, all excluded by the PRD
div_8x4 is still 3.20x of qjs; the second-stage target is met only on div_16x8 and mod_8x4
the directed vectors' event coverage was verified with temporary counters; the shipped test asserts correct results, not that a given vector still takes a given branch
pow is not measured, being a repeated mulAlloc and unrelated to division

next_denominator.profile_order_if_continuing: scratch allocation (four of the six are mergeable), the qhat division, normalization copies, building quotient and remainder together, the result wrapper/FAM, helper codegen
